description:
## Finding
\`pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs\` \`dfs\` (L185–268) terminates a path when an anchor's subject DN matches the current cert's issuer DN — only DN match, no SPKI match. The doc comment on \`build_path\` states \"Signatures are **not** verified here; that is the responsibility of the caller via [\`pkix_path::validate_path\`].\" — fair, but:

- A trust-anchor pool with two anchors having the same subject DN but different keys (key rollover scenario) terminates path building at whichever anchor matches first. \`validate_path\` is then called and may return SignatureInvalid if the wrong key was matched.
- pkix-path's \`validate_path\` correctly handles this case by trying every name-matching anchor (line 838–862). The path builder does not surface that ambiguity; it returns a single chain.

## Why P3
- Documented behavior, not a defect per the contract.
- The downstream caller (\`pkix_path::validate_path\`) does the correct thing, so no security failure.
- BUT: in a key-rollover scenario, \`build_path\` returns success and the caller sees \`SignatureInvalid\` on validate_path even though a valid path through the *other* anchor exists. Less debuggable than necessary.

## Fix
Two reasonable improvements (either; not both):
1. When matching anchors by DN, iterate all matches and try each; return the first that produces a chain whose terminating cert can be SPKI-verified by the anchor (use \`spki_key_matches\`-equivalent comparison).
2. Document this behavior more prominently in the API doc and in a dedicated section on key-rollover.

## Scope reference
\`pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:185-268\`, \`pkix-path/src/lib.rs:838-862\` (the corresponding correct loop in validate_path).
title: P3: pkix-path-builder build_path doc says shortest path returned; DFS does not verify anchor SPKI
